game: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

findings.question: Trial of the Sword exact floor/room count and structure
findings.answer: 54 total floors, split as: Beginning Trials = 13 floors, Middle Trials = 17 floors, Final Trials = 24 floors (13+17+24=54). Of these, 45 are combat/fighting floors and 9 are rest-stop floors (no combat, allow saving/cooking). This resolves the conflict in favor of the '54 total / 45 combat + 9 rest' source over the '51 total / 12+16+23' source, which appears to be incorrect. Detailed breakdown per Zelda Wiki: Beginning Trials floors 1-6 forest combat, floor 7 rest stop, floors 8-12 water-themed combat, floor 13 final chamber (Master Sword returned to pedestal, trial complete point). Middle Trials floors 1-4 shrine/platforming, floor 5 rest stop, floors 6-10 dark forest, floor 11 rest stop, floors 12-16 Guardian Scout floors, floor 17 final chamber. Final Trials floors 1-5 jungle/thunderstorm with Stal enemies, floor 6 rest stop, floors 7-11 volcano, floor 12 rest stop, floors 13-17 ice, floor 18 rest stop, floors 19-23 ruins with Guardians, floor 24 final chamber with seven Monks.
sources: https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Sword_Monk%27s_Shrine (the actual article; 'Trial of the Sword' redirects here; fetched via r.jina.ai proxy)
findings.notes: Both citations are pages on the same wiki (zeldawiki.wiki, the community wiki formerly on Fandom); content is internally consistent and highly detailed (specific enemy types per floor range) which suggests it reflects verified/datamined data rather than guesswork, but I could not reach a second, fully independent site (IGN, Zelda Dungeon, Fandom-hosted Zelda Wiki, Eurogamer, Polygon, GameFAQs, Thonky, TrueAchievements were all blocked by bot-protection, 403/402/404 errors, or CAPTCHAs during this session) to corroborate. Confidence set to medium rather than high for that reason.

findings.question: Master Sword upgrade after Trial of the Sword — exact stat changes (Attack, Durability)
findings.answer: The claim '60 Attack / 188 Durability' after Trial of the Sword appears to be INCORRECT, or at minimum unconfirmed and inconsistent with documented mechanics. The Master Sword's actual stats in Breath of the Wild are: base Attack Power 30, 'awakened' Attack Power 60 (this doubled state already exists in the base game near Guardians/dungeons/Malice/enemies with no Trial needed — it is not a Trial-of-the-Sword-exclusive number). Its in-game displayed base Durability value is 40 (unlike other weapons it does not break — instead it depletes an 'energy' pool and recharges after ~10 minutes; one source estimates roughly 11,400 cumulative damage dealt before the awakened state needs to recharge). No source found ties the number 188 to the Master Sword in any state. Completing Trial of the Sword does NOT change these Attack/Durability numbers. Instead, the documented effect of completing Trial of the Sword is qualitative: the Master Sword becomes permanently 'awakened' (i.e. it stays at 60 Attack and glows at all times, rather than only near enemies/Malice/dungeons), and firing the Sword Beam no longer depletes its durability/energy at all.
findings.notes: Single-wiki sourcing again (could not reach a second independent site for corroboration due to widespread bot-blocking this session). Confidence is medium: I'm fairly confident the '188 durability' figure is fabricated/wrong (it appears nowhere in the source and doesn't match the game's known 40-durability display for the Master Sword), but I could not independently triple-check the exact numeric figures (30/60/40/11400) against a second source.

findings.question: Champions' Ballad per-character quest/trial names for Teba, Riju, Yunobo, Sidon
findings.answer: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CORRECTION: Teba, Riju, Yunobo, and Sidon are NOT the direct quest-givers or trial-designers for the four champion side-quests in this DLC — that role belongs to four Sheikah Monks speaking through stone Monuments (one per region) that appear after the opening quest 'EX The Champions' Ballad' (in which Zelda directs Link to the Shrine of Resurrection, the 'Divine Beast Tamer's Trial' is fought using the One-Hit Obliterator against monster strongholds on the Great Plateau, and the weapon then splinters into 4 orbs that become the regional Monuments). The four per-character MAIN quests are named exactly: 'EX Champion Revali's Song' (Rito/Teba region, Monument in Tanagar Canyon/Hebra area), 'EX Champion Mipha's Song' (Zora/Sidon region, Monument near Akkala Highlands/Zora's Domain), 'EX Champion Daruk's Song' (Goron/Yunobo region, Monument in Eldin Canyon), 'EX Champion Urbosa's Song' (Gerudo/Riju region, Monument in East Gerudo Mesa). Each of these quests contains THREE named trials (completable in any order) that each unlock a hidden shrine and award one of four needed 'Emblems': Revali's Song → Tanagar Canyon Trial (shoot Dinraal's horn, unlocks Shira Gomar Shrine), Hebra Peak Trial (shield-surf glowing rings to Pikida Stonegrove, unlocks Kiah Toza Shrine), Flight Range Trial (shoot 4 targets, unlocks Noe Rajee Shrine) — reward emblem 'Medoh's Emblem'. Mipha's Song → Path of Light Trial (Akkala Highlands cliff, sunrise reflection, unlocks Kee Dafunia Shrine), Ancient Foes Trial (Upland Zorana, defeat 3 Guardian Skywatchers + 1 Guardian Turret, unlocks Sato Koda Shrine), Waterfall Rings Trial (Mikau Lake → Lulu Lake → Ploymus Mountain, unlocks Mah Eliya Shrine) — reward emblem 'Ruta's Emblem'. Daruk's Song → Igneo Talus Titan Trial (Lake Darman shore, unlocks Kamia Omuna Shrine), Glowing Rings Trial (Death Mountain summit, unlocks Sharo Lun Shrine), Glowing Ring Trial (fall into ring above Darb Pond lava, unlocks Rinu Honika Shrine) — reward emblem 'Rudania's Emblem'. Urbosa's Song → East Barrens Trial (defeat Molduking, unlocks Keive Tala Shrine), West Barrens Trial (Sand Seal ring course, unlocks Takama Shiri Shrine), Yiga Clan Hideout Trial (retrieve Sacred Orb from Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm, unlocks Kihiro Moh Shrine) — reward emblem 'Naboris's Emblem'. Each questline ends with an 'Illusory Realm' fight inside the respective Divine Beast against a fear-manifested Blight Ganon (Windblight for Revali's/Medoh, Waterblight for Mipha's/Ruta, Fireblight for Daruk's/Rudania, Thunderblight for Urbosa's/Naboris), rewarding the ability-cooldown upgrade. Teba/Riju/Yunobo/Sidon's actual involvement is as optional dialogue/flavor NPCs, not formal quest-log trial-givers: Teba has 'The Diary of Revali' appear in his home and can be asked about Revali; Riju reveals 'Urbosa's Diary' and, during EX Champion Urbosa's Song, tells Link the Yiga Clan stole the Sacred Orb needed for the Barrens trial from the Yiga Clan Hideout; Sidon appears in a recovered memory (as a child at Veiled Falls with Mipha) and, during EX Champion Mipha's Song, directs investigation to Ulria Grotto; Yunobo reveals he found 'Lord Daruk's training journal' in the Abandoned North Mine and keeps it at his house.
findings.notes: This is a substantive correction to the task's premise — the prior research brief's framing ('Monster Strongholds' as the per-character mechanism) actually describes the OPENING quest 'EX The Champions' Ballad' at Hyrule Castle/Great Plateau, not the four per-character questlines, which use Monuments + named Trials + shrines + Emblems instead. All sourcing is from a single wiki (zeldawiki.wiki), reached only via an r.jina.ai reader proxy since direct fetches to it and to every other candidate corroborating site (Fandom Zelda Wiki, IGN, Zelda Dungeon, Polygon, Eurogamer, GameFAQs) returned 402/403/404 errors or CAPTCHA walls this session, and the WebSearch tool's budget was exhausted before this task began. Confidence is medium: the content is highly detailed, internally consistent across 9 separate page fetches, and matches known BOTW quest-name conventions I recall independently, but is not independently corroborated by a second site.

findings.question: Champions' Ballad reward — is there a 'Champion's Tunic' upgrade?
findings.answer: No evidence found for any 'Champion's Tunic' reward or upgrade in The Champions' Ballad. Confirmed completion rewards checked across multiple wiki pages are: four ability cooldown-reduction upgrades (Revali's Gale+ reduces recharge to 2 min, Mipha's Grace+ to 8 min, Daruk's Protection+ to 6 min, Urbosa's Fury+ to 4 min), the Master Cycle Zero motorcycle-like mount (obtained after defeating Monk Maz Koshia in the Final Trial beneath the Shrine of Resurrection), a 'Picture of the Champions' item for Link's House, four Spirit Orbs (one per Illusory Realm shrine set... actually per-shrine, so potentially more), and four Emblems used only as quest-progression keys (not standalone rewards). No page, including the dedicated Champions' Ballad overview page and each of the four individual EX Champion Song quest pages, mentions any tunic, armor, or clothing-related reward. This strongly supports the prior pass's suspicion that the 'Champion's Tunic upgrade' claim was simply incorrect — likely a confusion with the separate, unrelated 'Champion's Tunic' cosmetic DLC armor piece included in the Expansion Pass's Pack 1 (Hero's Path Pack / Master Trials trove of amiibo-independent armor), which is awarded simply for owning the DLC / an early cutscene pickup, NOT as a Champions' Ballad completion reward.
sources: https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/EX_Champion_Revali%27s_Song, EX_Champion_Mipha%27s_Song, EX_Champion_Daruk%27s_Song, EX_Champion_Urbosa%27s_Song (fetched via r.jina.ai proxy)
findings.notes: This is an absence-of-evidence finding across several detailed source pages rather than an explicit 'no such reward exists' statement from a source, so confidence is medium rather than high. The note about a distinct 'Champion's Tunic' armor piece existing elsewhere in the Expansion Pass DLC (Pack 1) is from my own training-data recollection only and is NOT independently verified this session — flagging as low confidence within this finding; it should not be treated as confirmed, only as a plausible explanation for the origin of the confusion.

findings.question: Eventide Island treasure chest count — total and fixed vs. randomized
findings.answer: UNRESOLVED, and the premise itself is questionable. Checked the main 'Eventide Island' wiki page, the actual shrine-quest page 'Stranded on Eventide' (this is the real name of the shrine quest triggered on arrival — NOT 'Trial of Eventide', which exists as an empty/stub redirect on zeldawiki.wiki), the 'Korgu Chideh Shrine' page, and checked candidate NPC names (Rensa — actually an unrelated Dueling Peaks Stable worker with a horse-taming minigame; Cloyne — an unrelated NPC in Lurelin Village who runs a wager-based 'Treasure-Chest Game' minigame, not on Eventide Island). None of these confirm a 'stranded merchant' NPC on Eventide Island who asks the player to find lost treasure chests, nor any specific chest count. The actual documented shrine-quest objective on Eventide Island is to find and place THREE Ancient Orbs into three pedestals scattered across the island (one on a Monster Stronghold at the island's north tip, one on a Blue Hinox's necklace in the central jungle, one on Koholit Rock requiring Stasis) — not chest-counting. The wiki does independently confirm Eventide Island is one of only two locations in the game (the other being Cloyne's unrelated Lurelin Village minigame) where treasure chests respawn after being looted, implying chests there function as a renewable resource rather than a finite collectible with a fixed count. I could not confirm whether the game displays any tracked count of chests found on the island.
findings.notes: Recommend the downstream trophy designer treat the 'stranded merchant asking about lost treasure chests' premise as UNCONFIRMED / likely a conflation (possibly with Cloyne's Lurelin Village minigame, or with a different game/mod) rather than building a trophy around a specific chest count. No fixed number was found anywhere despite checking the shrine quest, the island overview page, and the two nearest-matching NPCs in the game.

Could not confirm the exact origin or existence of a 'stranded merchant NPC asking about lost treasure chests' on Eventide Island — this may be a mistaken premise from the original research brief; no fixed chest count could be found for the island under any framing.

Could not confirm whether completing Trial of the Sword changes the Master Sword's in-game *displayed* base Durability number (40) at all, only that it stops the Sword Beam from consuming durability/energy — the distinction between 'durability' and the sword's 'energy'/recharge mechanic in the game's own UI was not fully pinned down from available sources.

Did not verify whether the four Illusory Realm 'Blight Ganon' fear-fights differ in health/attack patterns from their original main-quest Divine Beast counterparts (relevant if a trophy references difficulty).

Did not verify the low-confidence recollection (mentioned only as a hypothesis) that a separate, unrelated 'Champion's Tunic' armor piece exists elsewhere in the Expansion Pass DLC — this needs independent confirmation before being used in any trophy text.
